critical_code_review_comments: Settings.toggleEmail() sends the FULL settings object on each toggle (`api.put('/settings', { ...settings, email_briefing: val })`) instead of just `{ email_briefing: val }`. Works today because PUT /api/settings performs $set with only provided fields, but it's chatty and races if other settings were modified elsewhere concurrently. Recommend narrowing the payload to `{ email_briefing: val }`.

send_email_raw() returns a boolean and swallows the underlying error message — POST /api/briefing/email surfaces a generic 502 'Não foi possível enviar o email'. Consider logging + returning the upstream status/body so ops can diagnose sender failures (rate-limit, quota, invalid recipient).

send_daily_briefings() uses a nice atomic claim pattern via `{last_briefing_email_date: {$ne: today}}` + `$set: {last_briefing_email_date: today}` to avoid double-send. Good. However, the claim is set BEFORE the send attempt — if the LLM or email provider fails, the user won't retry today. Acceptable trade-off, but note it in ops runbook.

SettingsInput's `email_briefing` is Optional[bool] with default None, and update_settings filters out None — meaning a client cannot explicitly PUT email_briefing=null to clear. Not a real issue (Boolean has no third state) but worth documenting.

The scheduler is started in-process (app.on_event('startup')) — safe today with a single worker/replica, but if backend scales horizontally the same cron job will fire in each replica. The per-user atomic claim mitigates duplicate emails, so this is safe by design. Add a comment/docstring so future maintainers don't remove the claim.

server.py is now ~1197 lines and includes email sending inline (build_briefing_html + send_email_raw + send_daily_briefings + scheduler). Modularization into `emails.py` / `scheduler.py` would improve readability but is not urgent.
